sentences.text: Rewasaurus minori is the only known species in its genus. It featured a slender snout with heterodont teeth and a toothless, pointed tip on its lower jaw. This dinosaur is distinguished by having a shorter upper tooth row compared to the lower, with a dentary tip nearly level with the teeth and at least five teeth in the premaxilla. The toothless tip of the lower jaw curves upward to a sharp point, forming a 13-degree angle between the upper and lower edges.

Rewasaurus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically from the Carnian to Norian ages, in the Tiki Formation of India. The genus name Rewasaurus honors the Rewa Basin in Madhya Pradesh, India, where the fossils were found, while the species name minori is derived from the Latin word for 'small'. Sulagna Sen and colleagues described this new genus and species in 2026. The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of an incomplete skull and an articulated lower jaw. This holotype specimen is housed at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur with the accession code IITKGPR1191.

Rewasaurus is classified as a dinosauromorph allied with silesaurids, which may represent the earliest ornithischian dinosaurs. Phylogenetic analysis by Müller (2025) places Rewasaurus within Sulcimentisauria as the sister taxon to Diodorus.
The environment where Rewasaurus lived was likely semi-arid with seasonal floodplains and rainfall.
